summary: Kin Cheung works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
King Chung Lo specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Leipzig University, studying under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.
King Pong Chiu is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Manchester under doctoral supervisor Jacqueline Suthren Hirst, earning his PhD (attested 2014).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indologist. He completed his studies at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under traditional teachers Madhusudana Nyayacarya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, Narmada Tarkatirtha, Panchanana Sastri, and Narayana Chandra Gosvami Nyayacarya, and under teachers Gopinath Bhattacharyya and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, later holding a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Tokyo Imperial University (~1891–1894), he held posts at Fourth Higher School, Otani University, and Kyoto University (Professor of Philosophy, 1912–1927), teaching Keiji Nishitani, Hajime Tanabe, and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu.

Kiyoaki Okuda (born 1938) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1967–1973). He later held posts at Shitennoji University (attested 1993) and as director at Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato (1907–1956) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Enga Teramoto, completing a BA in 1931. He later held posts at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).

Kiyoshi Okano (born 1956) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University as an associate professor (attested 2002) and as a professor (attested 2013–2024).
Kiyoshi Shimokawabe (born 1944) specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral coursework at Rissho University, where he subsequently held posts attested in 1990 and 2001.

Kiyotaka Kimura (born 1940), a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1968). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1983–2003) and served as President of Tsurumi University (~2003–2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1985–1989). He held positions at Hokkaido University (~1996–2004), Tohoku University (~2004), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama (born 1928) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Hosei University, Nagoya University, and the University of Tokyo (~1973–1989).

Klaus Karttunen (born 1951) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola at the University of Helsinki (PhD ~1985–1990). He held posts at the University of Helsinki and the Academy of Finland, later succeeding Parpola.
Klaus Mylius (1930–2025) was an Indologist. During his academic career, he held positions at Leipzig University (~1976–1992), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1993), and the University of Bayreuth.
Klaus Pinte is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and held a post there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn (born 1938) is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held faculty posts at the University of Giessen (~1971–1993) and the University of Göttingen (~1993–2004).

Klaus Wille (born 1953) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1996), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009, 2018–2020).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1993) and held a professorship at the University of Vienna (attested 2012–2013).
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Uppsala University by 2000, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk (attested 1999).
